newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan applauds Clinton, seeks active U.S. role.
newsitem.headline: Jordan applauds Clinton, seeks active U.S. role.

text.p: Jordan's King Hussein on Wednesday applauded U.S. President Bill Clinton's re-election and said he was confident Washington would do "whatever it can" to help achieve Middle East peace during Clinton's second term.

"I am very happy with these results," the king told a joint news conference with visiting Israeli President Ezer Weizman. "We have been watching (the election results) and I don't think we got much sleep last night."
"The United States has a major role, the most prominent role in this world, to play in terms of achieving our objective of comprehensive peace," he said.
He said that Russia, co-sponsor of the five year peace process started at a 1991 Madrid conference, and Europe both also had a significant role to play alongside Washington.

"I am sure that the times ahead will continue to see the United States, with the help and support and complimentarity of Europe and Russia, continue to do what ever it can to help us towards achieving our goal of a comprehensive peace," he said.
Information Minister Marwan Muasher welcomed Clinton's win, saying the president had been "very instrumental in pushing the peace process forward".
"We think that his re-election opens the door for a more active role by the U.S. and we would welcome this," Muasher told Reuters.
U.S.-sponsored Israeli-Palestinian talks are deadlocked over implementation of an Israeli troop pullback in the West Bank town of Hebron, home to 400 Jewish settlers and 100,000 Palestinians.

Jordan's relations with Israel, built on a 1994 peace treaty which ended a 46-year state of war, soured in September when the government of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu opened a tunnel near Moslem holy sites in Jerusalem, angering King Hussein who was granted a custodial role over the sites in the 1994 accord.
